title: Set mouse snap traps at the droppings: square to the wall, trigger end at the wall
instruction: Mice are running along both walls of this passage; the dark brown droppings mark their runs. Set the four snap traps (they are not armed) the way pest controllers do: one trap at each droppings patch, square to the wall, with its trigger end (the yellow pedal) toward the wall and no more than 8 mm from the skirting board.
context: Pest control workers (O*NET 37-2021.00) and building maintenance workers (49-9071.00) trap mice where droppings show they run. Mice keep to walls, so CDC rodent-control guidance says to set a snap trap with its bait (trigger) end next to the wall, the trap making a T with it, and the US National Park Service's snap-trap guide shows a single trap with its trigger against the wall: a mouse running along the wall meets the trigger from either side. A single trap laid parallel to the wall meets mice from one side only (a parallel set uses two traps, triggers outward), and one with its trigger out in the room is run past. Each trap's trigger end has to be found and turned to the wall. Here the traps are real size and not armed (the bail has sprung): the task scores where and how they are set. The 8 mm, 15 degree and 25 mm tolerances are this task's, chosen to be checked with a ruler and a set square.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A passage in a building at real size (1:1); the wall above the skirting boards is cut away so the arms can reach. Four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Floor: a light grey vinyl sheet fixed to the table, 340 mm (along x) by 500 mm (along y) and 2 mm thick, x 14.0 to 48.0 cm, y -25.0 to +25.0 cm. (2) Two skirting boards (the walls): fixed white-painted MDF boards 340 mm long, 15 mm thick and 62 mm tall, standing on the table against the floor's long edges from x 14.0 to 48.0 cm, the left one from y +25.0 to +26.5 cm and the right one from y -26.5 to -25.0 cm, so their faces are at y +25.0 and -25.0 cm and they stand 60 mm above the floor. (3) Four droppings patches: dark brown patches 20 mm along the wall by 10 mm (paint or a sticker, 0.5 mm thick) on the floor, each centred 10 mm from a skirting's face (so 5 to 15 mm from it): two along the left wall, centred at x 34.0 cm and x 43.0 cm (y +24.0 cm), and two along the right wall, centred at x 33.0 cm and x 44.0 cm (y -24.0 cm). (4) Four snap traps, all alike: standard wooden mouse snap traps, unarmed and loose, 25 g each. Each has a pine base 98 mm long, 45 mm wide and 10 mm thick; on its top a yellow plastic trigger pedal 25 x 22 x 3 mm centred 17.5 mm in from one end (the pedal end), a grey steel spring block 8 mm (along the length) by 36 mm by 7 mm across the middle, and the sprung steel bail, a U of 2 mm wire 39 mm wide, lying flat over the pedal half with its cross bar within 4 mm of the pedal end; 17 mm tall overall. The other end is the plain end. The traps lie base down in the middle of the floor with their long sides along x, centred at (x 30.0 cm, y +13.0 cm), (x 42.0 cm, y +13.0 cm), (x 30.0 cm, y -13.0 cm) and (x 42.0 cm, y -13.0 cm); the two at x 30.0 cm have their pedal ends toward the robot (-x), the two at x 42.0 cm away from it (+x). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state: the score is read from the traps as they lie at the last step; the traps are interchangeable. A trap is 'still' when neither its centre nor the midpoint of its pedal end moved more than 2 mm over the last 0.5 s. A trap is 'placed' when it is still and lies base down on the floor: its base tilted at most 10 degrees from level, pedal side up, and its lowest point within 3 mm of the floor's top. A placed trap is 'set at' a droppings patch when all three hold: (a) square: seen from above, the direction from its plain end to its pedal end is within 15 degrees of straight at the patch's wall (perpendicular to the skirting, pedal end toward it); (b) close: the trap's point nearest that wall (a corner of its pedal end when it is turned) is no more than 8 mm from the skirting's face (touching counts, and so does up to 3 mm of contact overlap reported by the simulator); (c) at the patch: the midpoint of its pedal end is within 25 mm of the patch's centre, measured along the wall (along x). Score = 0.25 x the number of patches with a trap set at them: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. A patch counts once however many traps are set at it, and no trap can be within 25 mm of two patches. Score 0 if no patch has a trap set at it. Every outcome: all four set 1.0; three set and the fourth 12 mm off the wall, turned 20 degrees, 30 mm along the wall from its patch or left in mid-floor 0.75; one wall's two set and the other wall's two laid parallel to the skirting, or set with their pedal ends out in the room (plain end at the wall), 0.5; two traps set side by side at one patch and the other two left where they started 0.25; the start (all four in mid-floor, parallel to the walls) 0. A trap upside down, on its side, standing on an end, leaning on the skirting, lying on another trap, held more than 3 mm up or moving earns its patch nothing. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, check each trap with a ruler from the skirting's face to its nearest point (8 mm or less), a set square against the skirting (15 degrees is 26 mm of offset over the trap's 98 mm length) and a ruler along the skirting from the patch's centre to the middle of the trap's pedal end (25 mm or less).
fidelity: Real-size traps, skirting and droppings marks; rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The traps are unarmed (the bail has sprung) and each is one rigid body, so nothing can snap: the task scores where and how the traps are set, not arming them. No mice, bait or wall above the skirting are modelled. The scorer sees only the traps, so a trap held still within 3 mm of the floor counts as lying there.
reset_notes: Lay the four traps back base down in the middle of the floor, long sides along x, centred at (x 30.0, y +13.0), (42.0, +13.0), (30.0, -13.0) and (42.0, -13.0) cm: the two at x 30.0 cm with their pedal ends toward the robot, the two at x 42.0 cm with their pedal ends away from it. The traps are interchangeable and stay unarmed; the floor, skirting boards and droppings patches are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
